componentIdea.title: Relationship Between Energy, Forces, and Fields

chapterOverview.guidingQuestion: How are forces related to energy?
chapterOverview.purpose: This component idea connects forces to energy. Forces are one way that energy transfers between objects and systems. Work describes the process of energy transfer when a force acts through a distance.
chapterOverview.centralIdeas: Work is the process by which forces transfer energy through motion. A push or pull that speeds up an object transfers energy to that object, while a force that slows it down transfers energy away. Both contact and non-contact (field) forces can transfer or store energy. Each interaction involves paired forces, and changes in motion or shape are evidence of energy transfer.

table.roleOfForces: Pushes and pulls make things move faster.
table.energyEffects: Faster speeds lead to bigger shape changes in collisions.

table.roleOfFields: Magnets can transfer energy without contact.
table.energyEffects: Energy transfers lead to changes in motion of both objects.

table.roleOfForces: Each interacting object exerts a force on the other.
table.roleOfFields: Systems can store or release energy in gravitational, magnetic, and electric fields.
table.energyEffects: Energy transfer occurs when forces do work or when field energy changes.

table.roleOfForces: Forces do work when they change the position of objects in the same direction as the force.
table.roleOfFields: Fields store energy and transmit it across space.
table.energyEffects: The amount of energy transferred depends on how far an object moves in the direction of the force.

progression.narrative: Understanding evolves from seeing pushes and pulls as causes of motion to recognizing them as mechanisms for energy transfer. Elementary students focus on contact forces; middle school students include non-contact fields and the concept of work; high school students quantify these transfers and apply conservation relationships.

standards.statement: Demonstrate how a stronger push or pull makes things go faster and how faster speeds during a collision can cause a bigger change in the shape of the colliding objects.
standards.bigIdea: Pushes and pulls can make things go faster. Faster speeds during collisions cause bigger changes in shape.
scientificIdeas: A push or pull can cause an object to move faster.
Pushes and pulls can differ in strength and duration.
Objects move at different speeds depending on the push.
Faster objects cause greater shape changes when colliding.
Collisions involve pushes in both directions on both objects.
Collisions that change shape tend to reduce the objects’ motion.
studentIdeas: The speed of an object depends only on its own properties.
Collisions happen too fast to count as pushes or pulls.
Only one object pushes in a collision.
Soft things change shape; speed is unrelated.
Walls and the ground aren’t 'objects' in collisions.

standards.statement: Evaluate how magnets cause changes in the motion and position of objects, even when the objects are not touching the magnet.
standards.bigIdea: Magnetic forces are non-contact forces that can change motion and transfer energy.
scientificIdeas: Changes in motion are evidence of energy transfer.
Forces are pushes and pulls with magnitude and direction; they transfer energy to or from objects.
Speeding up means energy is transferred to the object; slowing down means energy is transferred away.
Magnets exert forces without touching.
Magnetic interactions involve force pairs acting on both objects.
studentIdeas: Magnets only push or pull when touching.
Attraction and repulsion are not forces.
Objects moved by magnets have no energy.
Magnetic motion happens 'by itself.'
Magnets create energy from nothing.

standards.statement: Carry out an investigation to show how faster speeds during a collision can cause a bigger change in the shape of the colliding objects.
standards.bigIdea: Collisions transfer energy, changing shape, producing sound or heat, and altering motion.
scientificIdeas: Forces during collisions transfer energy.
Stronger pushes make objects move faster and transfer more energy.
Shape change, sound, or heat are evidence of energy transfer.
Collisions involve forces on both objects.
After collisions, objects may slow as energy transfers to surroundings.
studentIdeas: Shape changes aren’t related to energy transfer.
Energy is destroyed when motion stops.
Only one object experiences a force.
Heat and sound are unrelated side effects.
Hard objects never change shape.

standards.statement: Evaluate and interpret that for every force exerted on an object there is an equal force exerted in the opposite direction.
standards.bigIdea: All forces occur in pairs and can transfer energy to or from both objects in the interaction.
scientificIdeas: Interacting objects exert equal and opposite forces on each other.
Each force can change motion, showing energy transfer to or from both objects.
Energy can be stored by changing positions (stretching springs, lifting objects, separating magnets).
Work transfers energy when a force changes motion in the direction of the force.
Force pairs act as internal energy exchanges in a system.
studentIdeas: Forces act only one way during interactions.
Only the moving object changes energy.
Stored energy appears from nothing.
Newton’s third law applies only to still objects.
Forces only transfer energy when speeding things up.
